verses.1: As Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa thus conversed, the spring night arrived, which was neither cold nor hot.
verses.2: Then, in the clear morning, Rama, having completed his morning rituals and being knowledgeable about the citizens' affairs, proceeded to the audience hall.
verses.3: Then Sumantra approached Rama and informed him, "O King, these ascetics are standing at the door, having been stopped."
verses.4: These great sages, residents of the Yamuna bank and pleased to see you, O tiger among men, are eagerly requesting an audience with you, led by Chyavana, the son of Bhrigu.
verses.5: Hearing those words, Rama, the knower of dharma, commanded that the revered Brahmins, led by Chyavana, be admitted.
verses.6: Then, the doorkeeper, honoring the king's command by placing it on his head and with folded hands, admitted those ascetics who were otherwise very difficult to approach.
verses.7: More than a hundred great-souled ascetics, shining with their own spiritual radiance, entered the royal palace.
verses.8: Those Brahmins brought many offerings for Rama, including full pitchers honored with waters from all sacred pilgrimage sites, and various fruits and roots.
verses.9: Rama, showing great affection, received all those offerings, including all the sacred waters and various fruits.
verses.10: The mighty-armed Rama then addressed all the great sages, inviting them to take these excellent seats as was appropriate for their stature.
verses.11: Having heard Rama's words, all the great sages sat down on the beautiful, well-known golden seats.
verses.12: Having seen the sages seated there, Rama, the conqueror of enemy cities, reverently and with folded hands, spoke these words.
verses.13: He asked what the purpose of their visit was and what he could do for them attentively, declaring himself to be at the command of the great sages, ready to fulfill all their desires easily.
verses.14: Rama declared that his entire kingdom, his very life, and everything he possessed was for the sake of the Brahmins, and he spoke this truth to them.
verses.15: Having heard his words, a great applause arose from the sages of severe austerities who resided on the banks of the Yamuna.
verses.16: And those great souls, filled with great joy, said, "O best among men, such a statement is fitting only for you on earth, and for no one else."
verses.17: Many powerful kings who came before you, O King, considered the gravity of this task and did not undertake the vow.
verses.18: But you, out of respect for Brahmins, made this vow without considering the difficulty, and therefore you are indeed the one who will accomplish it, without a doubt, and you ought to protect the sages from great fear. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 60 ।। Thus ends the sixtieth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
